rules.title: Tenant owes all remaining rent on early termination (ignores duty to mitigate)
rules.description: Per § 47a-11a, if a tenant leaves early the landlord must make reasonable efforts to re-rent the unit at a fair rental to mitigate damages. A clause accelerating all remaining rent — making the tenant automatically liable for the entire balance of the term regardless of re-renting — is unenforceable to that extent.
rules.tenant_explainer: If you break your lease early, your landlord can't just bill you for every remaining month — they're legally required to try to re-rent the place. A clause demanding the whole remaining rent up front ignores that duty.

citations.label: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-11a
citations.quote: (a) If the tenant abandons the dwelling unit, the landlord shall make reasonable efforts to rent it at a fair rental in mitigation of damages. (b) If the landlord fails to use reasonable efforts to rent the dwelling unit at a fair rental, the rental agreement is deemed to be terminated by the landlord as of the date the landlord has notice of the abandonment.
